{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — FX Platform License Agreement (Licensor / Licensee)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel for the Customer/Licensee)  
**Re:** Playbook review — 18 verified findings (all verification: pass)

---

## 1. Executive summary

The Agreement is drafted heavily in the Licensor's favour and, as written, contains several terms that sit at or beyond our walk-away lines. Three issues are critical: (i) there is **no Licensor indemnity at all**, while Article XII imposes a broad one-way indemnity on us and Article XIII(a) affirmatively disclaims Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement claims; (ii) Article III vests **all** IP in the Licensor, including customization work we pay for under Article VII(b), with no reservation of our trading, order, client and account data; and (iii) Article XIII excludes consequential damages and caps liability **only for the Licensor**, at one half of amounts paid — below our six-months'-fees floor — leaving our own liability uncapped and unqualified by any Excluded Claims.

A further cluster of high-severity issues concerns lock-in and exit: a 36-month term with **no Licensee termination for convenience**, a Licensor-only unilateral **seven-year renewal option**, a licence grant that excludes our Affiliates and contractors and is revocable on any breach without cure, and an assignment/change-of-control regime that prohibits our assignment outright while permitting Licensor assignment (including to our competitors) and terminating the Agreement automatically on a Licensee change of control. Medium and low items — audit limits, the fixed support-fee commitment, the 36-month all-personnel non-solicit, absent transition/data-return mechanics, the pure "AS IS" warranty disclaimer, and the absence of any insurance covenant — are addressed by targeted redlines with fallbacks.

Five rules test **compliant** and require no redline: exclusivity, liquidated damages/penalties, non-compete, governing law and venue (New York law, exclusive New York state and federal courts), and MFN.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary / our position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | No Licensor indemnity anywhere; Article XII runs one way against us on very broad triggers, and Article XIII(a) disclaims Licensor liability for IP infringement claims. We add a Licensor defence/indemnity (third-party IP, breach of law, unauthorised access to Licensee data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice/control/cooperation and an express carve-out from the Article XIII exclusions and cap, and narrow our indemnity to Licensee-provided content and our breach of applicable law. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | Article III vests all right, title and interest in Licensor, and the "Derivative Work" definition (1.3) captures improvements; we own nothing we pay to have developed under Article VII(b) and no provision reserves our data. We carve out Licensee Data and paid-for customization deliverables, with a perpetual royalty-free licence back of embedded Licensor IP and no joint ownership, leaving Licensor's Platform ownership intact. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | Article XIII excludes indirect damages and caps liability for Licensor only, at one half of amounts paid; our liability is uncapped and expanded by Article XII. We make the exclusion and cap mutual, reset the cap to the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, and add Excluded Claims carve-outs (confidentiality/data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), confirming fee obligations are not capped damages. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | GENERAL PROVISIONS | Section (c) bars Licensee assignment outright with no Affiliate/successor carve-out while Licensor may assign freely; Article XX(a) auto-terminates on a Licensee change of control absent Licensor consent, deemed reasonably withheld if the acquirer competes. We make assignment mutual with an Affiliate/successor carve-out, bar Licensor assignment to our competitors, apply a not-unreasonably-withheld standard, and convert Article XX(a) to a notice obligation. Fallback: mutual assignment to successors on notice, consent not unreasonably withheld for other transfers. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | The grant runs to Licensee alone and access is confined to Licensee employees, excluding Affiliates and contractors; Article IV permits immediate termination for "any breach" with no materiality threshold or cure. We extend the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (subject to Field of Use and confidentiality), permit assignment to an M&A successor, and limit revocation to material breach uncured after 30 days' notice. |
| 6 | High | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | Article IV(I) lets Licensor unilaterally extend for a further seven years with no Licensee consent, reminder or pricing cap — and contradicts Article IV(II)–(III), which contemplate extension by mutual agreement. We convert to successive 12-month renewals declinable on 30 days' notice, with a 60-day reminder and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. Fallback: renewal only by mutual written agreement. |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | We are locked into a 36-month Initial Period with no convenience right; all termination triggers run in Licensor's favour. We add a 30-day Licensee convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, no early-termination charge or acceleration of Supplemental Payments, and confirm Licensor has no convenience right during the term. |
| 8 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | Grant is expressly non-exclusive and nothing requires us to source solely from Licensor. The Article XXII right of first refusal is a change-of-control right, not exclusive dealing. No redline. |
| 9 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties | Compliant | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | Fees are usage-based plus a monthly support fee, with no minimum spend, shortfall charge, acceleration or exit payment; Article XXIII bars termination damages. The audit cost-shift is reimbursement of actual cost. No redline. |
| 10 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § I CERTAIN DEFINITIONS For the purposes of this Agreement: | Article X contains only nondisclosure and employee non-solicitation; the Field of Use and Article II restrictions are licence-scope limits, not restraints on our business. The competitor element of the change-of-control consent is addressed under ASSIGN. No redline. |
| 11 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | 50+ US$5.00 | Article IV(b) permits Licensor-initiated audits with no frequency cap, no advance notice (the 30 days is our deadline to submit), no business-hours limit and no auditor confidentiality. Cost allocation and auditor selection are acceptable, so we add only frequency, notice, business-hours, confidentiality and no-system-access limits. |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Deviation | 50+ US$5.00 | Platform fees are usage-based with no volume floor, but the USD 2,500 monthly support fee is mandatory and non-reducible for the full 36 months (~USD 90,000) with no exit. We make the support services cancellable or reducible on 30 days' notice with pro-rated fees and confirm no minimum purchase commitment. Fallback: commitment limited to 12 months with a true-up. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | Article X(b) is one-way against us, runs three years post-termination and covers all Licensor and Affiliate personnel. The existing general-advertising and unsolicited-inquiry carve-outs are acceptable, so we take the fallback: mutual, 12 months, limited to personnel directly involved in the Agreement. |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION | Article XXI runs entirely in Licensor's favour (five-day return and certification by us); nothing requires Licensor to return our hosted market data, order and trade records or to assist on wind-down. We insert a new Article XXI-A: six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Licensee Data in machine-readable format within 30 days, then certified deletion. Fallback: 90 days. |
| 15 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | WARRANTY DISCLAIMER | Article VIX is a pure "AS IS" disclaimer of all express and implied warranties, including any commitment that nonconformity will be corrected. We insert a limited warranty (workmanlike services, 12-month conformity to Documentation, compliance with laws, no malicious code) with a repair/replace/refund remedy, carved out of the disclaimer. Fallback: 90-day conformity period. |
| 16 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | GENERAL PROVISIONS | Article XXIV(a) selects New York law with exclusive venue in New York state courts and the S.D.N.Y., plus venue and forum non conveniens waivers. No arbitration provision. No redline. |
| 17 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that: | No pricing-parity or most-favoured-nation obligation runs against us; commercial terms are fixed-rate or revenue-share. The "other licensees" reference regarding Revisions operates in our favour. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | GENERAL PROVISIONS | No insurance article; the only insurance reference is a cost pass-through to us. Licensor hosts the technology through which our market data and orders are transmitted. We insert a covenant at preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request). Fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These findings are expressly identified as at or beyond our playbook walk-away lines and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **No Licensor indemnity plus a one-way Licensee indemnity for Licensor's technology (INDEMN)** — the combination of the absent Licensor IP indemnity, the broad Article XII obligation on us, and the Article XIII(a) disclaimer of Licensor liability for IP infringement is the express walk-away scenario.
2. **One-sided liability cap at one half of amounts paid (LOL-CAP)** — below the six-months'-fees floor, with our own liability uncapped and no Excluded Claims.
3. **Assignment and change of control (ASSIGN)** — both limbs are at or beyond the line: a blanket one-way bar on our assignment, and automatic termination on our change of control at Licensor's discretion.
4. **Unilateral seven-year renewal at Licensor's option (RENEWAL)** — an automatic multi-year renewal without our consent.
5. **Unlimited, on-demand audit rights against us (AUDIT)** — no frequency cap, notice period or auditor confidentiality.
6. **Three-year, all-personnel non-solicit binding only us (NOSOLICIT)** — both duration and scope are in the walk-away zone; we have proposed the fallback rather than deletion.
7. **Pure "AS IS" disclaimer with no performance warranty (WARRANTY)**.

Items 1–3 are critical and, in our view, non-negotiable in substance. Items 4–7 have workable fallbacks already drafted.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering all 13 deviation/missing findings; the five compliant rules require no change and should not be reopened.
2. **Sequence the negotiation** around the three critical items first — Licensor indemnity with an express carve-out from the Article XIII exclusions and cap (without it, the indemnity is nullified), the mutual cap and Excluded Claims, and the IP carve-out for Licensee Data and paid-for customization deliverables.
3. **Bundle the lock-in package** (T4C, renewal, licence scope for Affiliates/contractors, assignment and change of control, support-fee commitment) as a single commercial trade, since together they determine our ability to exit and to integrate the platform across the group.
4. **Confirm the operational items** with the business: transition assistance and data-return timing for our hosted trading records, acceptable audit notice and frequency, and whether Licensor can meet the preferred insurance limits or requires the fallback.
5. **Escalate** to the deal principal if Licensor refuses the Licensor indemnity, the mutual cap, or removal of the change-of-control termination right, given their walk-away status.
6. **Re-run this review** against Licensor's turn to confirm the Article XIII carve-outs survive and that no new definitions (in particular "Derivative Work" and "Change of Control") are re-scoped in ways that reintroduce the issues above."}
